COMPUTER STUDIES OCTOBER — MOCK EXAM #18
====

GRADE: Grade 11
SUBJECT: COMPUTER STUDIES OCTOBER
TIME ALLOWED: 2 hours
TOTAL MARKS: 80
EXAM BODY: KNEC / KCSE pathway

INSTRUCTIONS
----
1. Answer all questions.
2. For calculations, show formula → substitution → steps → final answer with units.
3. For multiple choice, choose the best option.
4. Check your work before submitting.

SECTION A — MULTIPLE CHOICE
----
1. When learning Structured Query Language, the safest correct step is: (1 mark)
   A. Guess wiring or cutting steps for Structured Query Language.
   B. Leave sharp tools on the floor after Structured Query Language.
   C. Follow procedure, use tools correctly, and check safety for Structured Query Language.
   D. Skip safety briefings for Structured Query Language.

2. When learning Object Oriented Programming Concepts, the safest correct step is: (1 mark)
   A. Follow procedure, use tools correctly, and check safety for Object Oriented Programming Concepts.
   B. Leave sharp tools on the floor after Object Oriented Programming Concepts.
   C. Skip safety briefings for Object Oriented Programming Concepts.
   D. Guess wiring or cutting steps for Object Oriented Programming Concepts.

3. Electricity safety rule: (1 mark)
   A. Overload every socket
   B. Never touch live wires with wet hands
   C. Insert metal objects into sockets for fun
   D. Ignore burnt cables

4. When learning Relational Database Fundamentals, the safest correct step is: (1 mark)
   A. Guess wiring or cutting steps for Relational Database Fundamentals.
   B. Leave sharp tools on the floor after Relational Database Fundamentals.
   C. Follow procedure, use tools correctly, and check safety for Relational Database Fundamentals.
   D. Skip safety briefings for Relational Database Fundamentals.

5. When learning Logic Circuits, the safest correct step is: (1 mark)
   A. Skip safety briefings for Logic Circuits.
   B. Leave sharp tools on the floor after Logic Circuits.
   C. Guess wiring or cutting steps for Logic Circuits.
   D. Follow procedure, use tools correctly, and check safety for Logic Circuits.

6. When learning Logic Gates, the safest correct step is: (1 mark)
   A. Leave sharp tools on the floor after Logic Gates.
   B. Follow procedure, use tools correctly, and check safety for Logic Gates.
   C. Guess wiring or cutting steps for Logic Gates.
   D. Skip safety briefings for Logic Gates.

7. When learning Computer Network Standards and Protocols, the safest correct step is: (1 mark)
   A. Follow procedure, use tools correctly, and check safety for Computer Network Standards and Protocols.
   B. Leave sharp tools on the floor after Computer Network Standards and Protocols.
   C. Guess wiring or cutting steps for Computer Network Standards and Protocols.
   D. Skip safety briefings for Computer Network Standards and Protocols.

8. A computer’s main brain for processing is the: (1 mark)
   A. Speaker
   B. Monitor
   C. CPU
   D. Keyboard

9. ICT stands for: (1 mark)
   A. International Cricket Team
   B. Information and Communication Technology
   C. Internal Cooking Timer
   D. Input Cable Tester

10. When learning Binary Arithmetic Operations, the safest correct step is: (1 mark)
   A. Leave sharp tools on the floor after Binary Arithmetic Operations.
   B. Guess wiring or cutting steps for Binary Arithmetic Operations.
   C. Follow procedure, use tools correctly, and check safety for Binary Arithmetic Operations.
   D. Skip safety briefings for Binary Arithmetic Operations.

11. Before using a sharp tool in a workshop, you should: (1 mark)
   A. Run with the tool
   B. Work alone with eyes closed
   C. Wear safety gear and follow instructions
   D. Remove all guards

12. When learning Web Development Fundamentals, the safest correct step is: (1 mark)
   A. Skip safety briefings for Web Development Fundamentals.
   B. Guess wiring or cutting steps for Web Development Fundamentals.
   C. Leave sharp tools on the floor after Web Development Fundamentals.
   D. Follow procedure, use tools correctly, and check safety for Web Development Fundamentals.

13. When learning Object Oriented Programming Implementation, the safest correct step is: (1 mark)
   A. Leave sharp tools on the floor after Object Oriented Programming Implementation.
   B. Guess wiring or cutting steps for Object Oriented Programming Implementation.
   C. Skip safety briefings for Object Oriented Programming Implementation.
   D. Follow procedure, use tools correctly, and check safety for Object Oriented Programming Implementation.

14. When learning Network Security, the safest correct step is: (1 mark)
   A. Leave sharp tools on the floor after Network Security.
   B. Follow procedure, use tools correctly, and check safety for Network Security.
   C. Skip safety briefings for Network Security.
   D. Guess wiring or cutting steps for Network Security.

15. When learning Data Representation, the safest correct step is: (1 mark)
   A. Follow procedure, use tools correctly, and check safety for Data Representation.
   B. Skip safety briefings for Data Representation.
   C. Guess wiring or cutting steps for Data Representation.
   D. Leave sharp tools on the floor after Data Representation.

SECTION B — STRUCTURED / SHORT ANSWERS
----
16. In three clear sentences, explain Object Oriented Programming Concepts and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)

17. In three clear sentences, explain Object Oriented Programming Implementation and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)

18. In three clear sentences, explain Relational Database Fundamentals and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)

23. In three clear sentences, explain Logic Gates and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)
